notes: Draw every sprite at scale 0.5 (or load as @2x/resolution 2). Ground anchor (0.5,0.5) on the tile centre from toScreen(i,j); objects anchor (0.5,0.75) on the tile centre. Layers: ground < overlay < object (sort objects by i+j).

shore.rule: bit set when that neighbour is land. Clear a corner bit if either adjacent edge bit is set (N needs NW,NE clear; E: NE,SE; S: SE,SW; W: SW,NW). Reduced mask 0 = plain water; else file shore_<mask>.

shore_sand.appliesTo: water tiles whose land neighbours are beach sand
shore_sand.bits: same as shore (8-bit, corners reduced, 47 tiles)
shore_sand.rule: Compute the reduced shore mask exactly as for shore. Then count the land neighbours that set a bit in the reduced mask: if strictly more of them are sand than grass, use shore_sand_<mask>; otherwise (tie, majority grass, or any non-sand land) use shore_<mask>. Reduced mask 0 = plain water_a/b. Its land side has the same flat sand border as sand_a, so it meets sand_a and sand_edge_* seamlessly; water/foam/shallows match shore_* exactly, so shore and shore_sand tiles can sit side by side along the water.

sand_edge.rule: bit set when that edge neighbour is sand OR water (water counts as sand so the beach runs to the shoreline). Mask 15 -> sand_a; else terrain/sand_edge/sand_edge_<mask:02d>@2x.png (mask 0 = lone sand patch). Open sides fade into the shared grass background ~0.2 tile inside the tile with an irregular border, so the tile edge on an open side is plain grass and meets grass_a..f seamlessly. 4-bit set: no diagonal bits, so an inside corner where only the diagonal neighbour is grass stays sand.

forest_edge.rule: bit set when that edge neighbour is also forest. Mask 15 -> any of forest_a..d (interior); else forest_edge_<mask:02d> (trees thin out to bushes toward open sides; mask 0 = lone copse). Object layer over a grass tile, anchor (0.5,0.75).

road.crosswalks: on every arm of T (3-arm) and cross (4-arm) pieces
road.rule: bit set when that edge neighbour is road; mask 0 has no sprite (use a dead-end).
